contradicted: The dispatch's own leading hypothesis (PREBAKE-ENG ENG-03: a leading-zero normalization divergence between plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts's normalizeParcelKeyToken and parcel-geometry-resolver.ts:176's SQL regexp_replace) was falsified by direct query against hauska-prod-497015: every one of the 20 dispatch fixture ids has a stored parcelNodeId that matches the current txgio_parcel prop_id digit-for-digit, with zero normalization divergence. parcel-geometry-resolver.ts:176 is a geometry-pointer-resolution query (given an existing parcelNodeId, find its ring) and was never involved in the reconcile's key comparison. The write path said something else, per the dispatch's own invitation to falsify: reconcileCountyParcelNodes's set-difference math was never wrong; a single 2026-08-11 run fed it a catastrophically undersized plan (all 57,704 retirements share one identical timestamp and one templated reason naming the same vintage on both sides), and the function has no mechanism to ever reconsider a row once retired, so the bad run's damage was permanent even after the county was correctly and completely reloaded on 2026-09-03.
leave_behind: WHY the 2026-08-11 plan was undersized was not forensically traced to a root cause (no Factory runs ledger was reachable from ATOMS_DATABASE_URL to inspect that run's original CLI invocation/args). The fix does not depend on knowing why -- it makes a bad plan's retirements recoverable and gates recovery on live corroboration -- but whoever owns the parcel-node writer's operational practices should know a single CLI invocation can silently retire 92% of a county with no confirmation prompt and no plan-completeness sanity check before this fix; that structural gap (no circuit breaker on how much of a county's active set one run may retire) is named here but not built, since P-212's mission was recovery + guard, not a general write-path hardening pass.

The same defect CLASS (a reconcile treating an undersized plan as a real disappearance) has structurally always been possible on Hays, Caldwell, McLennan, Williamson, Travis and Ector too -- canon notes they hold 0/0/0/0/40/3,791 retired parcel-nodes respectively and 'the reconcile has only ever been run against Bastrop', so this specific incident hasn't recurred elsewhere, but nothing before this fix prevented it. review-retired-parcel-nodes.mjs's LIVE_CURRENCY_SOURCES registry is Bastrop-only today (parcelCurrencyFromBcadMap against the public Bastrop FeatureServer); the other five counties have no registered live source, so if any of their retired counts are ever found to include a false retirement, this CLI will correctly report candidates but reactivate none of them until a live source is registered for that county. Flagged, not built -- out of this mission's scope (Bastrop only, per PLAN-ROW P-212).

1,013 parcel-node atoms remain retired for county 48021 (up from the dispatch's single-id 77293 example). Every one was independently spot-checked in isolation (not just via the bulk 150-id-chunk BCAD query) and confirmed genuinely absent from the live county endpoint at time of this close. These may be real parcel losses, replats, or renumbering at the county since the underlying land was last observed -- not re-derived further, since establishing WHY each is gone is outside this mission's falsifiers (which only required 77293 specifically to stay retired, and it does).

The dispatch's own headline ('about 54,800... are live') is explainable as an extrapolation from the 20-id sample's ratio (19/20 = 95% * 57,704 ~= 54,819), not an independent measurement -- this lane's full-population live check found a higher live rate (98.2%, 56,691/57,704). Reported per AGENT_CONTRACT rule 5 (two numbers that should agree and don't = a free finding), not rounded off.
